_note: Fourth layer of the aliveness atlas (#6652): the inhabited world (animism). The world layer's rubric counts only matter itself said to be alive and rejected spirit-inhabited nature by design (421 judged rejections cited spirits, gods or personification), and its probes were learned European vitalist vocabulary. These phrases are what translators write for places, waters, mountains, trees, animals and the land treated as persons or as the homes of persons, and for the relations people keep with them (offerings, appeasement, offence). Matched as FTS5 phrases over the mirror's English translations (pages_en). Ambiguous phrases are kept on purpose ("fetish" is also Victorian polemic, "kami" also a Japanese word for paper or hair): the screen and the judge decide, and the outsider register is recorded, not dropped.
